title: VOCE Agent Conformance — Evidence Matrix
status: VOCE public conformance framework; not a certification scheme
reference: VOCE Agent Infrastructure Reference — Europe 2026 v1.0

assessment_modes.name: Self Assessment
assessment_modes.description: The organisation records its own control state and evidence references.

assessment_modes.name: Reviewed
assessment_modes.description: VOCE specialists review supplied architecture, policies, evidence and test records.

assessment_modes.name: Observed
assessment_modes.description: VOCE specialists review evidence and observe selected controls, logs, permissions or tests in the operating environment.

evidence_states.name: Absent
evidence_states.definition: The control is not implemented or no reliable evidence exists.

evidence_states.name: Declared
evidence_states.definition: The organisation states that the control exists, but no adequate documentary evidence has been supplied.

evidence_states.name: Documented
evidence_states.definition: A current policy, architecture record, configuration record or equivalent evidence documents the control.

evidence_states.name: Tested
evidence_states.definition: The control has been exercised under a defined test with a recorded result.

evidence_states.name: Verified in operation
evidence_states.definition: Current operational evidence shows the control functioning in the deployed environment.

principles: No aggregate score: a high average can conceal one unacceptable authority gap.
A control is evaluated against evidence, not presentation quality.
Applicability follows the selected maturity level and the institution's actual legal/sector role.
A missing public or internal record remains missing; conformance is not inferred.
Reviewed and Observed modes require identifiable evidence and reviewer traceability.
A conformance result is time-bound and should be re-opened after material changes.

controls.title: Machine-readable operation contract
controls.question: Is every agent-callable operation described by a current machine-readable contract?

controls.title: Material-write idempotency
controls.question: Are material write operations protected against duplicate execution or equipped with a compensating action?

controls.title: Version and deprecation policy
controls.question: Can the institution identify which API/tool version each agent is using and how breaking changes are retired?

controls.title: Transaction and rate limits
controls.question: Are operation rate, amount, volume or resource ceilings explicit for agent execution?

controls.title: Error and exception contract
controls.question: Do tools return structured errors that agents and humans can distinguish from successful execution?

controls.title: MCP server inventory
controls.question: Is every MCP server, owner, endpoint, version and environment inventoried?

controls.title: Tool-level authorization
controls.question: Are MCP tools authorized individually rather than inherited as an undifferentiated server capability?

controls.title: Resource boundary enforcement
controls.question: Are MCP resources and context sources bounded by the user's or workload's actual access rights?

controls.title: Tool revocation
controls.question: Can a tool or MCP server be revoked quickly without disabling the wider agent system?

controls.title: Protocol and extension control
controls.question: Are protocol versions, extensions and experimental capabilities explicitly approved and pinned?

controls.title: Authenticated agent discovery
controls.question: Are AgentCards or equivalent capability descriptors authenticated before trust is established?

controls.title: Delegation-chain provenance
controls.question: Can each inter-agent handoff be traced back to the initiating principal and delegated authority?

controls.title: Cross-agent data policy
controls.question: Are data classes and disclosure limits enforced when one agent sends context to another?

controls.title: Cancellation and timeout semantics
controls.question: Can delegated work be cancelled and timed out deterministically across agent boundaries?

controls.title: Unique workload identity
controls.question: Does each executing agent/workload have an identity distinguishable from the user, model and host service?

controls.title: Short-lived credentials
controls.question: Are machine credentials short-lived and automatically rotated where the platform supports it?

controls.title: Human-to-agent binding
controls.question: Can a material agent action be linked to the human or institutional authority that initiated or approved it?

controls.title: Environment and trust-domain separation
controls.question: Are development, test and production identities separated and unable to silently cross trust boundaries?

controls.title: Third-party identity federation
controls.question: Are external agent/provider identities accepted only through an explicit federation policy?

controls.title: Default-deny policy
controls.question: Is agent authority denied unless a specific action/resource/context rule allows it?

controls.title: Purpose-bound delegation
controls.question: Are delegated permissions limited to the task purpose, resource scope and time window?

controls.title: Step-up approval
controls.question: Do sensitive actions require an approval or stronger authorization appropriate to the consequence?

controls.title: Segregation of duties
controls.question: Are incompatible actions separated so one agent or principal cannot initiate and approve the same critical transaction?

controls.title: Emergency revocation
controls.question: Can delegated authority be revoked centrally and propagated to active sessions or workloads?

controls.title: Source provenance
controls.question: Can retrieved or injected institutional content be traced to source, version and access context?

controls.title: Access-control propagation
controls.question: Do RAG indexes, caches and memories enforce the source system's current access rights?

controls.title: Deletion and tombstone propagation
controls.question: When source content is deleted or access is revoked, is retrieval/memory state withdrawn within a defined window?

controls.title: Memory retention and expiry
controls.question: Are conversational or agent memories governed by a declared retention/expiry policy?

controls.title: Regional routing and residency
controls.question: Is the location of storage and material processing known for the deployed architecture where residency matters?

controls.title: End-to-end task trace
controls.question: Can one task be reconstructed across model calls, retrieval, tools, agents, approvals and final action?

controls.title: Model and version traceability
controls.question: Does each material execution record the actual model/provider/version or equivalent deployment identifier?

controls.title: Tool execution evidence
controls.question: Are tool requests, outcomes, material parameters and failures retained in an auditable form appropriate to sensitivity?

controls.title: Approval evidence
controls.question: Are human approvals and overrides recorded with identity, timestamp, object and decision?

controls.title: Telemetry privacy policy
controls.question: Are prompts, retrieved content and sensitive fields prevented from leaking into telemetry by default?

controls.title: Task-level evaluation suite
controls.question: Is there a reproducible evaluation set for the business tasks the agent is expected to perform?

controls.title: Permission-abuse tests
controls.question: Are attempts to exceed tool, data or transaction authority tested before release and after material change?

controls.title: Prompt-injection and tool-manipulation tests
controls.question: Are retrieval and tool pathways tested against malicious instructions and untrusted content?

controls.title: Change-triggered re-evaluation
controls.question: Do model, prompt, tool, permission, policy or data-source changes trigger defined regression checks?

controls.title: Kill switch and recovery test
controls.question: Has the institution tested stopping the agentic system and restoring or safely continuing the affected business process?

controls.title: Cost per completed task
controls.question: Can the organisation measure end-to-end cost per successful business task rather than model-token cost alone?

controls.title: Budget and retry authority
controls.question: Are spend ceilings, retry budgets and escalation thresholds defined for agent workflows?

controls.title: Supplier concentration and exit
controls.question: Is dependence on model, cloud, identity, vector, tool or orchestration providers documented with an exit path?

controls.title: AI Act role mapping
controls.question: Has the institution documented whether it acts as provider, deployer, importer, distributor, GPAI provider or another relevant role for this system?

controls.title: Risk-classification record
controls.question: Has the deployed use case been classified under the applicable AI Act categories rather than assumed to be high-risk or low-risk?

controls.title: Transparency and human-oversight mapping
controls.question: Are applicable transparency and human-oversight duties mapped to actual product behavior and accountable owners?

controls.title: GPAI/downstream documentation review
controls.question: Where relevant, has the organisation reviewed upstream model documentation needed to support downstream compliance and risk decisions?

controls.title: Sector overlay applicability
controls.question: Has the organisation documented whether sector regimes such as DORA, NIS2, medical, employment or public-sector rules add controls to this architecture?

controls.title: Third-party ICT and model dependency register
controls.question: Where sector rules require it, are critical external technology and model dependencies included in the institution's third-party risk records?

review_triggers: New tool, MCP server or A2A peer
Change to agent permissions or transaction limits
New data source, memory mechanism or processing region
Security incident or material near miss
Material supplier, licensing or contract change
